newsitem.title: UK: Supermarket group Safeway enters Ireland.
newsitem.headline: Supermarket group Safeway enters Ireland.

text.p: British supermarket group Safeway Plc said on Thursday it had agreed to form a joint venture with Fitzwilton Plc to establish Safeway as a major grocery retailer in Northern Ireland and the Republic of Ireland.
The joint venture will acquire nine stores and four sites from Fitzwilton for a total of 65 million pounds ($106.6 million), together with initial stock valued at nine million pounds.
The new company, Safeway Stores (Ireland) Ltd, will be 50 percent each owned by Safeway and Fitzwilton.

It plans to take a further six stores under licence with options to purchase. The aggregate sales of the 15 stores being acquired were 148 million pounds ($242.7 million) in 1996, a market share of 11 percent in Northern Ireland.
Safeway is to assume full operational control of the stores over the next six months and they will be converted to the Safeway brand over the next 18 months at an estimated cost of 50 million pounds.
Safeway will safeguard the jobs of over 2,000 staff in Fitzwilton's Wellworth stores and new stores planned in Bangor, Cookstown, Downpatrick and Dungannon will provide a further 1,000 jobs.

The partners will each contribute an initial 10 million pounds of equity capital and the balance of the funding requirements will be debt financed. The venture is expected to break even this year after financing, before charging a total of some 10 million pounds of launch costs over the next three years.
